en: The *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-uttamarāja-sūtra*:
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling at the Bamboo Grove (Veṇuvana) together with the yakṣa Vajrapāṇi.
At that time, Śata-datta approached the World-Honored One;
having arrived, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet,
withdrew, and sat to one side.
The Heavenly Emperor Śatakratu addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
when I enter the ranks of battle to engage in combat,..."
"By means of the power of the asuras' delusive spells, incantations, and medicinal herbs, have they not been brought to defeat?
Indeed, it is so. I pray that the World-Honored One, out of compassion for me, will cause the asura hosts' delusive spells, incantations, and medicinal herbs to be crushed and subdued."
He skillfully expounded the most supreme mantra of the Great Secret.
Then the Bhagavat addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying:
"Kauśika, it is so; it is even so."
Kauśika, when engaged in battle with the asuras,
one may indeed be defeated through the power of vidyā-mantras, secret mantras, or medicinal herbs.
Out of compassion, I shall now explain this vidyā-mantra.
When one desires to cause delusion and confusion, it causes [the enemy] to retreat and disperse; battles, strife, and litigation are all completely extinguished.
All secret mantras and various medicinal substances are thereby brought to an end.
He spoke of the vidyā-mantra.
At that time, the Bhagavān spoke this Great Golden Light Vidya-mantra, saying:
"I shall now explain for you the three incalculable eons."
Various other practitioners of external paths wander everywhere,
giving rise to evil thoughts and creating all manner of obstacles;
I have come from that place, and I am able to subdue all their deceptions and secret spells.
The six perfections are fulfilled.
One cuts off all other non-Buddhist practitioners, the afflictions of wandering through various forms,
and the spells of logic, secret mantras, medicinal charms, as well as the great vidyā-mantras of all factions of Māras.
"Kauśika, you should accept and uphold this most supreme great secret mantra for the sake of gathering in all sentient beings.
The Lord of Devas replied:
"So be it, World-Honored One;
we shall receive your instruction accordingly.
At that time, the World-Honored One...
Then he spoke the Great Illuminating Mantra of Gold, saying:
Tadyathā | oṃ hinihini |
Hīlī hīlī, jīvilī jīvilī, hībhilī.
Nihī nihī nihī rabhi niñjana-paditthaṃ.
Bhudiccha mandara adikṛtti bitti bitti.
Bhinda mandalādikaraṭi hana hana.
Hā va hā va jinḍe jinḍe pinne pinne.
Bhagavati-jaye vijaye jambhani stambhani.
Bandhani mahaṇi amogha śodhi.
Dharani-kṛi-na-kṛi-ṇa-kā-ta-na-ma-na-pa-bha.
Cāṃpāya cāṃpāya, pañcāya pañcāya, siddhampāya.
Siddhya panta ya panta ya mahaya mahaya, all that exists.
Whether it be the illusions of devas,
the illusions of nāgas,
or the illusions of yakṣas.
Whether it be the illusory delusions of rākṣasas,
the illusory delusions of kiṃnaras,
or the illusory delusions of gandharvas.
Whether it be the illusions of asuras,
the illusions of mahoragas,
or the illusions of mahoragas with large bellies.
Whether it be the delusive power of a vidyādhara mantra,
the delusive power of a vidyādhara-king who has attained accomplishment,
or the delusive power of a ṛṣi.
Whether it be the delusions of all vidyā-mantras,
the delusions of sentient beings,
or all delusions whatsoever.
ra ra ra ra ra jāya jāya duma duma du dumāḥ /
Rava rava ravana cakṣu-lan-dan.
Galantha nihanahana sarvavidya.
Śatru-nan-si-tan-pa-ya-xiu-yian-si-tan-pa-ya.
Sūnaṣṭambhāya bhalu naṣṭambhāya aṇḍīniṣṭambhāya.
Ugraṃdara dāri dāri lidhaḥ
Ratnividhāraṇīpraśāntiḥ.
Bheṣajye 'tha bhaiṣajya,
if there should be those who act as my enemies, thieves, or those possessed by anger and malice, who contend and dispute excessively, wishing to do all manner of harm— haṇa haṇa!
Ṭaha ṭaha bāja bāja bañjaya bañjaya.
Camba ya camba ya sitamba ya sitamba ya bandha ya bandha ya.
Muhāya muhāya mahāmuhāni bhagavati saṃgha.
May you protect me from all fears, afflictions, and epidemics! *Cundā svāhā*, O Kauśika!
Whether it be a son of good family or a daughter of good family...
If a king or a royal minister can recollect this Vidyā-mantra of the Golden One,
they shall have no fear of others.
Within that faction, they cannot be harmed or disturbed by the enemy armies of others,
nor by devas, nor by nāgas, nor by yakṣas, nor by gandharvas.
Nor are they asuras, nor are they kinnaras, nor are they mahoragas.
Nor are they holders of vidyā-mantras,
nor are they the Sky-Flying Mothers (Ḍākinīs) and the like;
nor can they be harmed by any life-sustaining mantras, secret spells, or medicinal herbs, even when used at an improper time.
The opposing armies of others cannot invade or surround him;
the opposing armies of others do not harm his life;
and weapons cannot injure him.
Neither water, fire, poisons, mantras, secret spells, nor any medicinal substances can harm it;
rather, it returns to the very place where one has committed, taught, or rejoiced in the commission of evil deeds.
Kauśika, for this reason,
monks and nuns, as well as laymen and laywomen who possess pure faith, [should...]
If good sons and good daughters take this vidyā-mantra and recite it over water seven times,
they can wash their own bodies and thereby protect themselves.
If there are those who wish to transcend all fears, all afflictions, all epidemics, all vidyā-mantras, all secret spells, all medicinal herbs, and all malevolent sorcery and curses.
One should then recollect this *vidyā-mantra* of the Golden One.
Whether it be a king or a royal minister,
if they wish to crush the enemy host or subdue the enemy host, [they should do so].
One should also keep in mind this luminous mantra of gold.
If one recites it over a thread seven times and ties seven knots, then fastening it upon the body,
or if one recites it over water seven times, one will be able to protect oneself.
If there is one who writes down this "Dhāraṇī for Being Unobstructed Amidst All Fears," or is able to receive and uphold it,
or ties it beneath the shins, or places it upon a high banner when entering an army formation;
May Shan’an obtain liberation.
By the majestic spiritual power of this golden mantra,
may Shan’an’s inner kin and retinue be entrusted to his care, and may he transcend [all obstacles].
That which is unaccomplished shall be accomplished.
If one wishes to subdue those who possess vidyā-mantras,
one should recite the mantra seven times over a white thread and tie seven knots in it.
It can bind and subdue.
If one wishes to destroy various illusions and delusions,
one should take earth from a cemetery, recite the mantra over it seven times, and then scatter it.
It can destroy illusions and delusions.
When engaged in debate or competition, if one wishes to silence the opponent,
one should take *qin*, *chui*, or *li* roots, recite the mantra over them seven times, and then chew them.
One will be able to respond to all discourse;
for those who receive, uphold, read, recite, and praise it,
all transgressions will be entirely extinguished.
Furthermore, regarding those who have constructed that place or are contemplating it,
or those who protect themselves by binding it with ropes or water—
[the result accrues] to their bodies.
Above all,
no incantations, secret mantras, or medicinal herbs can cause harm;
that which has not yet been accomplished will all be brought to completion.
All that he sought was granted in accordance with his wishes.
When the Bhagavat had finished speaking this sutra, Śakra,
Lord of the Devas, having heard what the Buddha taught, received it with faith and practiced accordingly.
One fascicle of the *Suvarṇa-dhāraṇī-sūtra*.
